key_insight: Gate3DGen selectively cleans up real-world images before they reach a 3D generator, while leaving clean inputs unchanged. It aims to improve input quality without retraining the generator or losing visual cues needed for 3D reconstruction.
problem_solved: Single-image 3D generators perform well on curated images but struggle with uneven lighting, blur, and occlusions. Pre-processing must address these degradations without unnecessarily altering clean images or removing useful details.
method: Place a selective pre-processing model upstream of an existing single-image 3D generator.
Use a degradation-aware router to decide whether an input needs purification or should bypass processing.
Preserve visual cues important for 3D generation while correcting degraded inputs.
impact: This approach could make existing 3D-generation pipelines more reliable on everyday photos without generator retraining. The supplied abstract is truncated, so detailed mechanisms and quantitative improvements are not available.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image → degradation-aware router → purification or bypass → existing 3D generator.
Paired input examples showing uneven lighting, blur, and occlusion alongside clean images.
Routing illustration contrasting a clean-image bypass with a degraded-image purification path.
Conceptual detail-preservation graphic highlighting visual cues that should survive pre-processing.
paper_title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
paper_authors: Xiaolin Li, Zihao Huang, Fanpeng Meng, Chen Yang, Guanjun Wu
